A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Wonderland and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original camera-guided video generation and 3D reconstruction experiments, including benchmark comparisons and architectural and training-data ablations in Tables 1, 2, A2, and A3.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds an encoder fine-tuning comparison in Section 4.3 and Table 3.

M1.justification: Figure A3 revises the reported LoRA camera encoder: v2 replaces v1's normalization/activation stages and final zero-linear layer with a zero-initialized 3D convolution before 2D patchification. The overall dual-branch conditioning, LaLRM, losses, and progressive training remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same dataset and task coverage: RE10K, ACID, DL3DV, Tanks-and-Temples, Mip-NeRF scenes, and generated in-the-wild images/videos. The added encoder comparison introduces no new domain or task.

E2.justification: The external benchmark comparators remain unchanged. Within the reconstruction comparison, v2 Table 3 adds a jointly fine-tuned 3DVAE-encoder variant alongside the existing RGB-14, RGB-49, and frozen-encoder LaLRM configurations.

E3.justification: The reported DL3DV training stride changes from {1,2} to 1, and its evaluation stride changes from 2 to 1. Camera-error averaging changes from all generated frames to the first 16 frames, except MotionCtrl's 14 frames. These are protocol revisions; the unchanged benchmark scores do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds an ablation testing whether jointly fine-tuning the video encoder helps reconstruction, finding that freezing it performs better. The corresponding reconstruction ablation drops DL3DV results while retaining RE10K and Tanks. The appendix LoRA, ControlNet, and synthetic-training-data analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: V2 Table 3 adds fine-tuned-encoder PSNR results of 26.14 on RE10K and 20.75 on Tanks, compared with retained frozen-encoder values of 27.10 and 22.66. The earlier DL3DV reconstruction-ablation entries are removed. Table 1, the main benchmark rows of Table 2, and Tables A2–A3 retain identical scores. Appendix D.2 also newly reports that COLMAP-derived reconstruction poses outperform conditioning poses.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective, Plücker representation, reconstruction loss, and tokenization mathematics are retained. Equation numbering, notation-table additions, and relocation of architectural formulas to Appendix D do not introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: camera-controlled video latents, dual-branch conditioning, and feed-forward latent-to-3DGS reconstruction for high-quality, wide-scope single-image scene generation. The principal novelty and performance claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds explanations connecting latent reconstruction quality to perceptual/adversarial encoder pretraining and the information loss from aggressive RGB patchification. Section 4.3 interprets encoder fine-tuning as compromising the latent representation. Appendix E newly acknowledges costly model development and occasional generated motion that harms reconstruction.

D1.justification: V2 adds details about training-pose normalization, baseline pose-prefix selection, evaluation frame windows, and COLMAP-derived poses for reconstruction. It explicitly identifies the frozen reconstruction encoder and revises the detailed camera-encoder diagram. Most model sizes, optimization settings, training budgets, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 60 to 119 entries, beyond publication-metadata updates. Sections 1–2 and Appendix C substantially broaden coverage of camera control, feed-forward reconstruction, and static/dynamic generation, adding works such as AC3D, CameraCtrl II, Long-LRM, and Bolt3D, plus discussion of training-free camera control.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods, experimental narrative, conclusion, and appendices receive extensive paragraph-level rewriting. V2 expands the latent-reconstruction motivation, moves detailed tokenization descriptions into Appendix D, standardizes terminology and headings, and adds acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 reformats Figure 4, preserving square ZeroNVS outputs, redraws Figure A3, and separates the former Table 2 ablation block into a paired-entry Table 3. Appendix figures and the expanded notation table are relocated. Most visual examples and the overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 better supports the frozen-encoder choice through Table 3, documents evaluation more fully, and gives clearer explanations and more candid limitations. These provide a modest overall improvement. The gains are tempered by removal of DL3DV ablation results and protocol revisions that are not reconciled with unchanged benchmark scores; the PDFs do not establish improved headline performance.
